learning_outcomes.description: Apply expert knowledge of medicines gained throughout the program to improve person-centred health outcomes and reduce the risk of medicine-related harm to patients.

Use effective communication skills to comprehensively consult patients and clinicians (healthcare professionals) with patient-centred medicine information and care in a range of simulated pharmacy practice scenarios.
Identify, evaluate and justify the clinical significance of medication related problems in complex patient case scenarios.

Develop patient-centred medication management plans to resolve medication-related problems in complex patient case scenarios by referring to evidence-based clinical evidence (literature and tools) and the patient's context and goals.
Contribute to team-based care by expertly communicating and working with other members of the healthcare team in complex patient case scenarios.
Apply a model of ethical decision making to identify and propose practical, patient-centred solutions to ethical problems in complex patient case scenarios.
Demonstrate teamwork behaviours as appropriate to the roles of pharmacists within health care teams, including oral and written communication.

assessments.task_description:
This is a team assignment with a team mark awarded. Tutorial groups will be split into teams of 3 to 4 students. Each student team will be assigned an integrated case for which they will outline medication-related problems and their resolution. The assigned cases will be posted on Blackboard during week 9, after the mid-semester examination. 

Each student will be expected to present a 5-10 minute presentation of their case, and then answer questions from the audience.

Guidance regarding how to structure the student grand round team presentation and marking rubric will be provided on Blackboard. You will have the opportunity to ask questions about your cases and the student grand round during the tutorials in weeks 9 and 11.

Presentations will be assessed using the marking rubric by the course-coordinator.

This Presentation may be recorded, and the resulting recording retained as per university policy. The recording will be stored in a secure manner and will only be accessed if required for the purposes of moderation of marking; provision of feedback to the student; and/or re-marking following a successful re-mark application.

assessments.assessment_title: Over-the-counter (OTC) and Ethics OSCE oral exam
assessments.task_description:
The PHRM4012 OSCE oral exam will consist of 3 OSCE stations:

  • Over-the-counter counselling station, product request (5 minutes)
  • Over-the-counter counselling station, symptom-based request (5 minutes)
  • Ethics station (10 minutes)


Further descriptions, guidance and marking criteria for these stations are available on the PHRM4012 Blackboard site.

The PHRM4012 OSCE stations will be based on concepts, medicine disease states, medicines, scenarios, skills and knowledge you have attained during your pharmacy degree. 

This Oral Exam will be recorded, and the resulting recording retained as per university policy. The recording will be stored in a secure manner and will only be accessed if required for the purposes of moderation of marking; provision of feedback to the student; and/or re-marking following a successful re-mark application.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Submission: The exam will be held in-person at Dutton Park campus.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to defer this exam.
assessments.additional_info: You may be able to defer this exam.

assessments.task_description:
The oral examination will assess knowledge and application to identify medication related problems and discuss therapeutic decision making in choosing options to resolve the medication related problems.

This will be an oral VIVA of a patient case during the end of semester examination period.

The viva will be 25 minutes in duration including 10 minutes reading and preparation time. During the preparation and reading time only, you will have access to the AMH and eTGs. You will need to bring your own physical hard copy of the AMH.

You will then commence the oral examination which lasts 15 minutes, discussing the medication related problem(s) you have identified and plan to resolve these with the examiner who will then also ask you questions about your case and recommendations.

This oral viva will be recorded and retained as per university policy. The recording will be stored in a secure manner and will only be accessed if required for the purposes of moderation of marking; provision of feedback to the student; and/or re-marking following a successful re-mark application.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Submission: The exam will be held in-person at Dutton Park campus.

learning_activities.topic:
Practice roleplay (OTC) simulation

OTC practice cases and OTC notes will be provided on the course site for students to undertake self-directed practice. On tutorial weeks the course coordinator will be available for 1hr after the tutorial in the same room to answer questions.

Students are encouraged to practice taking a patient history and counselling their simulation patient during their study time with these cases.

The aim of these cases is to will allow students to practice and hone their skills in medication history taking and counselling for over-the-counter ailments and products in role play activities with or without their peers.


Learning outcomes: L01, L02

learning_activities.topic:
Skills Modules

Content for the weekly skills modules will be available on the course site to allow students to undertake self-directed learning on three topics; ethics, communication, and pharmaceutical calculations. On tutorial weeks the course coordinator will be available for 1hr after the tutorial in the same room to answer questions. 

Skills modules are aimed at improving core pharmacy practice skills. They will include modules on assertive communication strategies in difficult professional situations, educating patients on medicines and devices, discussing ethical dilemmas applying an ethical framework to decision making, and applying knowledge of pharmacy calculations to derive appropriate formulations and safe dosing recommendations.

Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06

learning_activities.topic:
Patient Centred Integrated Cases

Participants will work in small groups on complex patient cases to identify and assess medication-related problems, the reason for the problem, develop and review a management plan for the patient including research of evidence in the literature to consider other options to resolve the problem and justify your management plan. Participants will also be expected to discuss the role of other key healthcare professionals and communicate medication-related problems and solutions to improve the care of the patient in the case.

Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04, L05, L07
